From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus \"Codrus\"). \"Romanization of Ancient Greek\"):\\xa0*Andraímon*) may refer to:\\n\\n* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus \"Oxylus\") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) \"Dryope (daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon \"Calydon\"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. (daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

(daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus.
